question: Does extending transfer monitoring into lowering require a different grasp contract?

contract.transfer-only: Monitor transfer: bilateral contact, cube_z > 0.12m, grasp_error < 0.05m; age < 60ms.
contract.reuse-transfer: Use the same transfer predicate and age limit in transfer AND lower.
contract.phase-aware: Transfer predicate unchanged; lower requires bilateral contact and grasp_error < 0.05m, without the lift-height requirement. Age limit unchanged.
contract.release: All policies stop grasp monitoring at commanded release; successful placement is checked independently from physical logs. Release safety is not certified.
contract.stop: Bad captures spanning >=40ms or capture age >=60ms latch target hold. Decision is after the physics step; held actuator target applies at the next tick. No resume, replan or recovery budget in this experiment.

design: 21 deterministic cells: seven conditions x three policies, one rollout per cell. Same initial state and absolute simulation schedule. No randomized success-rate estimate.
hypotheses: A transfer height predicate may falsely stop normal lowering.
Removing only the lower-stage height requirement may permit normal lowering while retaining contact/error/age monitoring.
An uncontrolled drop over the tray may satisfy final placement without establishing a correctly monitored execution.
metrics: fault-to-stop latency where a stop follows fault onset
scope: Privileged MuJoCo contact/state observations, one clock, fixed phases. No camera, ROS2, learned policy, physical robot, regrasp, or full-task safety guarantee. Hypothesis support is separate from artifact validity.
